thread:
customer-jira-bot: New ticket from AcmeCorp: users seeing sporadic 200-500ms baseline but tail spikes to 2-8s on /v1/embeddings during sustained traffic. They set max_batch_size=128 on dynbatch and use mixed small/large payloads.

leo_support: thanks, grabbing details. Do they see any dimension mismatch errors or just latency/timeouts?

customer-jira-bot: No dim mismatch logs. A few 504s reported during spikes. Payloads: clients send 1-4 vectors per request, some clients send 200-vector bulks occasionally.

leo_support: quick hypothesis: large intermittent requests can cause batching to wait for fill to reach max_batch_size which increases tail latency if coalescing window is long. Also dynbatch may prioritize throughput -> head-of-line delays. Can you ask for their dynbatch config and sample request rates?

aimee_platform: They pasted config: `dynamic_batching: enabled, max_batch_size: 128, coalesce_window_ms: 40, prefer_latency: false, shard_policy: round_robin`

leo_support: aha. coalesce_window_ms=40 + prefer_latency=false + big max_batch_size = recipe for oscillation. If a few clients send huge bursts, small steady requests can sit waiting or get interleaved inefficiently.

dan_eng: can you get a short repro we can run? ask them to run this script hitting a single model variant:

customer-jira-bot: they ran a repro and attached timings. Short repro we gave them:
```bash
# burst small steady stream + occasional large bulk
for i in {1..500}; do
  python3 -c "import requests; print(requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'inputs':[ [0.1]*1536 ]}).status_code)" &
  if (( i % 50 == 0 )); then
    python3 -c "import requests; print(len(requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'inputs': [[0.1]*1536 for _ in range(200)]}).json()))" &
  fi
  sleep 0.02
done
```

leo_support: nice repro. can we see server-side router logs/snippets around a spike? infra-bot, any visible queue length or batch formation logs? :eyes:

infra-bot: log extract (anonymized):
```
[2801010123] dynbatch: accept req id=0x9a2 size=1
[2801010123] dynbatch: accept req id=0x9a2 size=1 -> queued (queue_len=12)
[2801010124] dynbatch: accept req id=0x9b3 size=200 -> queued (queue_len=13)
[2801010124] dynbatch: forming batch target=128 -> picked ids [0x9a2..0x9b3] total_size=201 -> scheduled (waited_for_fill=39ms)
[2801010124] runtime: exec batch size=201 -> split into 2 execs (128,73) -> exec1 latency=120ms exec2 latency=930ms -> tail returned 840ms after head
```

leo_support: that log shows exactly the issue: batch formation waited about 39ms to hit fill, then had to split into executions because batch > max effective exec size causing a long tail on the split part. Splitting large mixed batches causes KV cache inefficiencies and memory thrash -> long exec on second split.

aimee_platform: recommended mitigation steps we gave customer:
- lower max_batch_size to 64 or 32 for models with long per-token exec time
- set prefer_latency=true or reduce coalesce_window_ms to 5-10ms to favor latency over throughput
- enable small_request_preempt=true so big bulks don't starve small requests (if on Dedicated/Private)
- if they need high throughput for bulks, route bulks to a separate variant pinned to larger workers (model-routing by request-size)

dan_eng: got it. also suggest adding `max_batch_tokens` or an overall token cap so mega requests don't blow up batch memory.

customer-jira-bot: applying changes now (lowering max_batch_size->32, coalesce->8ms, prefer_latency=true). Will monitor for next 2 hours and report.

leo_support: thanks — ask them to include a short A/B timeline (before/after 95th/99th percentiles) and attach a small log slice if spikes persist. If tail still appears, we'll inspect kernel-level exec times and KV cache misses.

customer-jira-bot: quick follow-up: after change 1 hour in, 95p dropped from ~650ms to ~210ms, 99p from ~2.1s to ~420ms. They still see occasional 700-900ms spikes but much rarer.

leo_support: great improvement. next steps if they want to optimize further: dedicated route for bulk uploads + quantized model variant for bulks, or tune shard_policy to avoid head-of-line on hot shards. I'll convert this thread to a short KB note with recommended defaults. :white_check_mark:
